subject: Durable furniture for daily commercial use
hook: Commercial furniture rarely fails in the middle. It fails at the edges.
ig:
Commercial furniture rarely fails in the middle. It fails at the edges.

In an office, salon or staff room, furniture gets used more in a week than a home sideboard sees in a year. When we plan commercial pieces, these are the places we specify with care:

Front edges. Bags, chair arms and knees hit them constantly. A thicker ABS edge on the leading edge copes far better.

Plinths. Mops and hoovers find them every day. A recessed plinth with a tough edge avoids chips.

Hardware. Staff kitchen doors open all day. Soft-close comes as standard, which takes the slam out of every use.

Surfaces. Woodgrain and textured finishes forgive light scuffs better than plain gloss.

Fixings. Anything people lean on must be properly secured.

Save this if you're writing a spec for a workplace, and find our commercial cabinet making via the link in bio.
fb:
If you've ever seen a reception desk with a chipped front edge or a staff kitchen with a battered plinth, you'll know where commercial furniture wears first.

When we build for offices, salons and staff areas, we pay extra attention to the bits that take the knocks: thicker ABS edging on front edges, recessed and well-edged plinths, soft-close hinges and runners, forgiving woodgrain or textured finishes on busy surfaces, and solid fixing to the wall.

It's all made in our Hanley workshop for businesses across Stoke-on-Trent and Staffordshire. More about our commercial cabinet making here:
